Subject: POC success criteria & trial plan - Nova Analytics

Thanks for the call this morning — quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth before the kickoff. High-level ask from Nova: validate that Redwood can (a) meet your latency and throughput requirements for real-time scoring, (b) keep inference unit cost under your target, and (c) maintain answer quality for your extraction/slot-filling flows.

Proposed POC scope (3 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): data ingest & access (Nova provides sample CSV + schema; Redwood sets up private eval workload)
- Week 1 (baseline): run current model on Redwood default config, capture latency/throughput/cost and quality on provided eval set
- Week 2 (opt): iterate on batching, KV cache settings, and model variant (quantized) to optimize cost and latency while monitoring quality
- Week 3 (report): final metrics, regression check, and handoff documentation

Suggested success criteria (please review):
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 350 ms for median request size (~120 tokens); p99 < 600 ms
- Throughput: sustained 50 req/s at 10 concurrent workers for 512-token window without >1% 5xx errors
- Cost: average effective cost/token <= $0.0007 (target) across the workload after batching/kv cache
- Quality: automated pass-rate >= 92% on intent+slot extraction (provided test set) and human-annotated mean rating >= 4.2/5 on 100 sampled responses

Ownership & asks: 
- Nova: deliver sample CSV (10k rows preferred), schema, and 100 manually labeled examples for human eval by Wed 3/11
- Redwood: provide eval harness (redwood_eval_script_v1.py), initial runs, and a POC report by end of Week 3
- Internal owners: Karthik (POC lead, contact, quality gate), Ben (infrastructure & capacity), Marissa (customer ops & timeline coordinator)

Attachments: poc_scope_and_timeline.pdf (detailed timeline), redwood_eval_script_v1.py (test harness), nova_poc_data_sample.csv (sample placeholder — please replace with full sample)

Next steps:
1) Emma to confirm acceptance of targets and share data access details by EOD Wed 3/11
2) Redwood to schedule a 30-min kickoff (I propose Thu 3/12 9:00 AM PT)
3) Weekly sync cadence (Mon 30-min) during the run; ad-hoc for regressions

Thanks — I'll hold the kickoff slot tentatively until we hear back.

—Karthik

Agree with the targets overall. Couple of suggested tweaks from an ops perspective: 
- Latency target: lower p95 target to 300ms if we consistently hit <300 on baseline runs; otherwise keep the 350ms guardrail
- Throughput: define a short soak test (2 hrs) at 50 req/s to validate no memory growth and stable p99 latency
- Error budget: allow a soft error budget of 0.5% for transient 5xx during heavy upgrades; anything >0.5% triggers rollback and investigation

I'll take point on scheduling and the initial meeting invite. Ben — can you provision a dedicated sandbox pool for this test (4x A100 equivalent nodes) and confirm by EOD Wed 3/11?
